title: The Protocol of New Lagos
premise: Isandro Vane, a terraformer and cargo hauler in the contested orbits of New Lagos, discovers that the colony's children are all dreaming the same dream — a signal from the derelict relay at the edge of dead space, carrying the memories of the colony's dead founders. The colonial authority wants the signal silenced to protect the fragile peace treaty, but Isandro realizes it contains her mother's voice and the truth about who the colony was built on. Racing the closing jump window, she must choose between duty to the living and loyalty to the dead. She reaches the relay, broadcasts the founders' testimony instead of destroying it, and returns to a colony that must finally grieve — finding love with fellow hauler Teodoro Mbaye along the way.
about_author: Dominic Hartwell is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade aboard container ships before turning to fiction. He writes about people who keep distant places alive through routine, signal, and stubborn care.

chapters.title: Greenhouse Hours
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Between cargo runs, Isandro tends the seed vault meant for colonists not yet born, trading dry banter with Teodoro over comms. When a child asks her why the garden hums at night, she dismisses it — until she hears the hum herself. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness cracked open by first wonder.

chapters.title: The Shared Dream
chapters.summary: POV alternating between Isandro and nine-year-old Ama Okafor, who describes a dream of a woman standing in vacuum, singing. Forty-one children report identical dreams; the colonial authority calls it mass hysteria. Isandro recognizes the singing voice as her mother's. Emotional beat: dread braided with longing.

chapters.title: Manifest Irregularities
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Digging through seven years of shipping manifests, Isandro finds sealed cargo runs to the relay — runs her mother piloted before dying there. Authority officer Sefu Danjuma warns her off, offering a promotion as bait. Emotional beat: suspicion hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Teodoro's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Teodoro. A veteran hauler hiding his own grief for a brother lost near the relay, Teodoro agrees to fly Isandro out — if she promises they come back alive. They plan the run against the jump window: eleven days until dead space closes for a year. Emotional beat: two guarded people choosing trust.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. They slip out under a falsified ore manifest while Danjuma's patrol ships sweep the lanes. In transit, the children's dreams intensify — now the whole colony dreams, adults included. Isandro begins dreaming her mother's final hours. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by guilt.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: POV Teodoro. Past the last beacon, the ship goes dark-running through debris fields of the Founders' War. Systems fail; they drift silent for six hours, close enough to touch. Teodoro confesses his brother answered this same signal and never came home. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in fear.

chapters.title: The Relay Speaks
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Docking with the relay, Isandro finds its archive intact: recordings proving the founders seeded New Lagos on an inhabited world and erased its native minds — her mother among those who tried to stop it and were exiled to die here. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as wound.

chapters.title: Danjuma's Interception
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Danjuma's cutter catches them at the relay; he orders the archive destroyed to preserve the treaty and the children's safety. Isandro refuses. Standoff in vacuum while the jump window ticks down to minutes. Emotional beat: duty versus conscience at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Isandro transmits the founders' testimony colony-wide during the standoff, letting every dreamer hear the truth in their own language. Danjuma stands down rather than fire on a channel the whole colony is listening to. They burn for the window as it closes. Emotional beat: catharsis — grief spoken aloud at last.

chapters.title: What the Garden Grows
chapters.summary: POV Isandro, epilogue-flavored. Weeks later, the colony holds its first memorial for the erased and the exiled; the children's dreams have softened into ordinary sleep. Isandro replants the vault with seeds renamed for the lost, and stays — with Teodoro, with the garden, with the truth. Emotional beat: rootedness earned through rupture.
